# Results — Study 664 (ESG Premium)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **ESG
investing pays a premium** ("doing well by doing good"), or the skeptical counter-claim that
any ESG-fund edge is a **relabelled large-cap growth/quality tilt**. Offline & deterministic
once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30**
(the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).*

**Documented expense-ratio drag, no fitting:** ESGU costs **5.5 bps/yr more** than SPY
(0.150% − 0.095%); SUSA costs **22.0 bps/yr more** than IVV (0.250% − 0.030%). This drag is
already embedded in each fund's own realized NAV return (the prices used are already net of
it) — it is quoted here as the *structural* explanation for roughly a third of SUSA's raw gap
and essentially all of ESGU's, not as a further deduction.

## The headline — tracking difference & Sharpe

| quantity | ESGU vs SPY (2016-12 → 2026-06, n=2,402d, 9.5y) | SUSA vs IVV (2005-01 → 2026-06, n=5,387d, 21.4y) |
|---|--:|--:|
| CAGR (fund vs benchmark) | +15.31% vs +15.45% | +10.50% vs +11.09% |
| Ann. volatility (fund vs benchmark) | 18.59% vs 18.23% | 18.28% vs 18.85% |
| Excess-of-cash Sharpe (fund vs benchmark, same ^IRX rf) | **+0.730** vs **+0.747** | **+0.543** vs **+0.561** |
| Tracking error (annualized) | **3.75%** | **4.78%** |
| Information ratio | **−0.015** | **−0.135** |
| Active return (annualized) | **−0.057%** | **−0.644%** |

Both ESG funds trail their plain-vanilla benchmark by a hair on CAGR and Sharpe — but they
also carry **real basis risk** (3.75% / 4.78% annualized tracking error) for that hair of
underperformance. This is the first sign the "premium" isn't showing up even before formal
inference.

## Active-return spread test — long ESG fund / short benchmark, daily

| quantity | ESGU − SPY | SUSA − IVV |
|---|--:|--:|
| n (days) | 2,402 | 5,387 |
| mean active return | **−0.023 bps/day** (−0.057%/yr gross) | **−0.256 bps/day** (−0.644%/yr gross) |
| Newey-West *t* (5 lags, **primary**) | **−0.08** | **−1.07** |
| Welch *t* (cross-check) | −0.01 | −0.11 |
| net of costs (2 legs × 5 bps one-way + 30 bps/yr borrow) | −0.378%/yr | −0.953%/yr |
| hit rate (days fund beat benchmark) | 50.2% | 49.9% |

Neither spread clears |*t*| ≥ 2 in **either direction**. ESGU vs SPY is statistically
indistinguishable from a coin flip (hit rate 50.2%, *t* = −0.08); SUSA vs IVV drifts negative
but stays short of the certification bar (*t* = −1.07). **No premium, and — just as
importantly — no statistically detectable penalty either.**

## Factor decomposition — is any gap a growth/value or quality tilt?

Daily fund return regressed on [benchmark return, growth−value spread (IVW−IVE), quality
spread (QUAL−benchmark)], Newey-West (5-lag) HAC standard errors.

| quantity | ESGU (mkt = SPY) | SUSA (mkt = IVV) |
|---|--:|--:|
| raw active return (annualized) | −0.057%/yr, NW *t* = −0.08 | −0.644%/yr, NW *t* = −1.07 |
| factor-model alpha (annualized) | **−0.064%/yr**, NW *t* = **−0.09** | **−0.187%/yr**, NW *t* = **−0.27** |
| growth-value beta (IVW − IVE) | **+0.025**, *t* = **+3.63** | +0.001, *t* = +0.14 |
| quality beta (QUAL − benchmark) | **+0.109**, *t* = **+3.41** | **+0.247**, *t* = **+8.50** |

Both funds carry a **statistically significant, real quality tilt** (β on QUAL−benchmark:
*t* = 3.41 and 8.50 — this is not noise), and ESGU additionally carries a small but
significant growth tilt (β = 0.025, *t* = 3.63; SUSA's growth-value beta is indistinguishable
from zero, *t* = 0.14, because its ESG methodology screens rather than tilts by sector). But
because the *raw* active return was never significant to begin with, "controlling for the
tilt" doesn't kill an alpha — there was no alpha to kill. For SUSA the point estimate shrinks
from −0.644%/yr (*t* = −1.07) to −0.187%/yr (*t* = −0.27) once the quality tilt is priced in —
about **70% of the raw gap is quality-factor beta**, not stock-picking skill (positive or
negative). The honest reading: **ESG funds are measurably quality-tilted (and ESGU mildly
growth-tilted) large-cap portfolios that neither outperform nor underperform their benchmark
by a statistically detectable amount.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic correlated-return world (fund vs benchmark, correlation 0.97) with a TUNABLE
planted daily premium; no network.

| world | NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (premium = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.43** (sd 0.88), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted premium = +5.0 bps/day (seed 664) | mean active +4.198 bps/day, **+8.73** |

The detector never fires on the null and lights up on a planted premium. *(A faithful-engine /
power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Neither ESGU−SPY (NW *t* = −0.08, hit rate 50.2%) nor SUSA−IVV
  (NW *t* = −1.07, hit rate 49.9%) clears |*t*| ≥ 2 in either direction across a combined
  9.5-year and 21.4-year sample. ESG investing shows **no statistically detectable premium —
  and no statistically detectable penalty either.** The point estimates are both mildly
  negative but not certifiable.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no edge to trade: the active-return spread nets further
  negative once the (small but real and *documented*) higher expense ratio, one-way trading
  costs and a short-borrow drag are charged, while tracking error of 3.75–4.78%/yr is real,
  uncompensated basis risk carried for zero expected payoff.
- **"Any ESG return difference is really just a growth/quality tilt?" — CONFIRMED.** Both
  funds carry a statistically significant quality-factor beta (*t* = 3.41, 8.50) and ESGU a
  small significant growth beta (*t* = 3.63); ~70% of SUSA's (statistically insignificant)
  raw underperformance is quality-factor beta, not selection. The honest picture is a
  large-cap index fund with a documented sector-screen-driven quality/growth tilt bolted on —
  not a source of alpha, positive or negative.
